To what end?  This isn't really an interface that was intended to be used by more than one subscriber. Is there something you're trying to get done by putting this here?

- it's a commonly used interface with many usages [1]

- it's used as part of new code [2], so we cannot make any argument that it's somehow deprecated

- it's an actively developed interface with new methods like `UpdateFruField` being added [3].

- openbmc documentation [4] states that

 > D-Bus interfaces are defined in the `phosphor-dbus-interfaces` repository


> Is there something you're trying to get done by putting this here?

I want to enable existing compatible interfaces to be usable via PDI generated bindings. So we can get them documented as either

- acitively used and developed
- deprecated and no new usages to be added because of some issue with the interface
- legacy interface, ok to use but not actively developed

For a deprecated interface we could then point people to another interface to be used instead as replacement. Without proper documentation in PDI i don't see how that's to be done.

References:
[1] https://github.com/search?q=org%3Aopenbmc+%2F%28%3F-i%29ReScan%2F&type=code
[2] https://github.com/openbmc/platform-init/blob/c9c8612b9cdccc232311ca12ebd25b9f4a08491f/nvidia/nvl32.cpp#L334
[3] https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/entity-manager/+/80889
[4] https://github.com/openbmc/docs/blob/41d0c7a722d6bd05baaf49d37647942559b42c50/CONTRIBUTING.md?plain=1#L385

Why? Fru-device is an internal interface within entity-manager. 

If we’re going to make this public, by documenting it here, we have to also be willing to make changes to align with the rest of the interfaces. I gave a top level “configuration” tree for unchanged entity-manager interfaces that don’t conform because there are a lot of users and baggage and hoped that we could refactor them. I’ve generally not accepted “well we did this thing outside of the process and now we want to document it” interface proposals otherwise.

> Why? Fru-device is an internal interface within entity-manager. 

Wrong. `ipmid`, `intel-ipmi-oem`, `fb-ipmi-oem`, `ampere-ipmi-oem` all use the `GetRawFru` method.

https://github.com/search?q=org%3Aopenbmc+%22GetRawFru%22&type=code

For `ReScanBus` it is mostly meta platforms who use it as part of scripts

https://github.com/search?q=org%3Aopenbmc+%22ReScanBus%22&type=code

> I’ve generally not accepted “well we did this thing outside of the process and now we want to document it” interface proposals otherwise.

If you do not review ongoing works then of course people will be free-wheeling their way through your design intent.

If it's merged, it's part of openbmc. It's not a proposal. It's an existing interface.

And if we do not document it, how are folks going to consume it with PDI.

So person A worked outside the process, person B refuses to document existing interfaces, 

and now person C is stuck without the tooling support and must hand-code everything without a generated client.

#### precedence and guiding examples

You can also think about it this way. People usually find some code which registers a method on an interface and then they copy that to define a new method.

If we establish a pattern whereby we at least get the interface name, object path namespace and such from PDI, it becomes clear that interfaces and their methods and properties are defined in the PDI.

If we refuse to document existing stuff, we reinforce the pattern of folks doing things outside of PDI because that's what they find in the code.

> If you do not review ongoing works then of course people will be free-wheeling their way through your design intent.

Is there a problem you're alluding to?  fru-device was written long ago now when a whole company did a lot of "freewheeling".

> So person A worked outside the process, person B refuses to document existing interfaces, and now person C is stuck without the tooling support and must hand-code everything without a generated client.

I don't see how "person B" is the one to blame in this?  Alternatively if I just let whatever in, why bother with having reviews here?  Why bother with having any process?  Doesn't that just encourage people to do their own thing?

Ultimately "Person A" is the one to blame; unfortunately they're not around any more.  That means "Person B" and "Person C" have to clean up the mess.  Are you willing to do the interface definition and refactoring?

> If we refuse to document existing stuff, we reinforce the pattern of folks doing things outside of PDI because that's what they find in the code.

We also reinforce a pattern of not following process.

> I don't see how "person B" is the one to blame in this? Alternatively if I just let whatever in, why bother with having reviews here? Why bother with having any process? Doesn't that just encourage people to do their own thing?

I do not want to blame anyone here, but if the point of PDI is to interact with dbus interfaces then it does not work if some interfaces are somehow exempt from it for non technical reason.
Let's not make life hard for person C.

That's just another argument people then use to say they do not want the PDI in their repo since it does not even support my_special_interface.

#### ongoing works

> Alternatively if I just let whatever in, why bother with having reviews here?

Currently the `WriteFruFromFile` method is in review and already got two +1.
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/entity-manager/+/83992

The review about the interface should happen when the interface is added, right?

#### halfsies

Having the review at a later point makes it so that there are two reviews and then we end up with half-way support of something.

Now where the interface is added first, PDI or in the reactor, that's a question between maintainers. That's something to clear in ToF.


#### process

> We also reinforce a pattern of not following process.

If maintainers are not capable to follow project design intent then project is already doomed. Since project is not (yet) doomed i hope they can follow. 

Maintainers are *in their own category* and *should be aware of project design intent*.

But with help and support for existing interfaces it should be easier to follow,
especially for people new to the project who base their contributions around existing code.

> We also reinforce a pattern of not following process.

Most people who go around the PDI are not usually the ones who push for PDI adoption. They do not necessarily have something to gain from this support since they do not use the PDI anyways.

#### no intent to re-design a working interface

> Are you willing to do the interface definition and refactoring?

I want to support the existing interfaces in PDI, to the extent that they can be supported (may be limitations due to usage of variant).

If the existing interfaces cannot be supported in PDI then it will be hard to introduce PDI into existing asio reactors as the maintainers will not see a use-case in adding a dependency and refactoring external interfaces just to add such dependency.

I do *NOT* want to refactor dbus methods with 10s of upstream and probably 100s of downstream callers just for a re-design of a method which is already functional and working today.

I'm aware it is probably in the wrong namespace and should likely not be toplevel interface.

But that's how it is defined.

#### PDI role in refactoring

Without PDI, dependency of a repo on a specific interface is only discovered at runtime, if you are lucky, you can grep for it.

With PDI, the refactoring and estimating scope of work becomes easier.

So if anyone in the future wants to refactor `xyz.openbmc_project.FruDeviceManager` into something else, it will be easier to have all the callers use PDI since
a simple build will expose what will break.

Breaking the build is also a good way to communicate any interface changes to downstream.

So if the project goes 

pdi interface -> refactoring -> solution

it should be less breakage than

refactoring -> pdi interface -> solution
Closing this discussion thread since the existing interface has already been merged, and past design decisions are not magically undone by introducing incompatibilities.

Marking as -1 until https://github.com/openbmc/technical-oversight-forum/issues/54 is resolved, since you decided to go that route.

I don't see any plan to refactor interfaces, so I am not in favor of this direction.  My previous policy has been that I'm not blindly accepting dbus interfaces that people wrote elsewhere without org-level review.  I don't see sufficient evidence to sway from that past policy.
